name: CIS Critical Security Controls
description: The CIS Critical Security Controls v8 is a prioritized set of 18 Controls (153 Safeguards) for defending against pervasive cyber attacks. v8 reorganized from v7.1's 20 Controls into 18, consolidated some, and added cloud and mobile-specific safeguards. Safeguards are organized into three Implementation Groups (IG1 ⊂ IG2 ⊂ IG3) representing increasing levels of cybersecurity maturity required to implement them. Each Safeguard specifies its asset type (devices, software, data, network, users), security function (identify, protect, detect, respond, recover), and applicability per Implementation Group.
relationToCloudSecurity: CIS Controls v8 added explicit cloud security safeguards in IG2/IG3 (e.g., Control 4 — Secure Configuration of Enterprise Assets and Software — includes safeguards for cloud-native configurations). Maps to CSA CCM, NIST CSF, and ISO 27001 via the published CIS Mappings.
relationToAISecurity: CIS Controls v8 does not specifically address AI workloads. AI systems that store, process, or transmit organizational data remain subject to CIS Controls regardless of implementation technology. CIS has not yet published AI-specific control extensions.

license.notes: Licence verified 2026-11-13 on cisecurity.org, Terms of Use for Non-Member CIS Products (https://www.cisecurity.org/terms-of-use-for-non-member-cis-products): "The CIS Controls and associated guidance documents in accordance with the Creative Commons Attribution-Non Commercial-No Derivatives 4.0 International Public License". Under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 Section 2(a)(1), anyone may reproduce and share the Licensed Material, in whole or in part, for non-commercial purposes only, with the attribution Section 3 requires; and may produce and reproduce Adapted Material for non-commercial purposes only, but never share it. Section 2(a)(4) allows the technical modifications needed to use the material in other media and formats, and says such modifications never by themselves produce Adapted Material. A mechanical conversion of CIS's XLSX to JSON, CSV or Markdown is such a format change, so a copy that only changes format may be shared non-commercially with attribution like the original; anything that alters, abridges or rearranges the content beyond format would be Adapted Material and may not be shared. publicly_redistributable is false for a separate reason: the source XLSX is downloaded from CIS WorkBench after registration, which makes this a Tier 3 source under the 4-tier hosting rule (Kurt Seifried, 2026-11-09). Public mirroring of a Tier 3 source needs Kurt's approval, and none has been given. Since 2026-11-13 this public repository holds only this metadata stub. Corrections 2026-11-13: earlier metadata recorded CC-BY-4.0, and the README said CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, which is the licence CIS states for the PDF CIS Benchmarks; a first correction overstated the NoDerivatives restriction by treating format conversion as adaptation.

lifecycle.notes: v8 was current 2021-2024. v8.1 (June 2024) is now the active version with minor updates. v8 remains widely referenced in compliance documentation. The changelog extraction (cis-controls-v8-changelog.json, held in the private dataset) maps v8 → v7.1 for organizations migrating from older versions.

current_extraction.notes: This describes the extraction held in the private dataset (dataset-private-laws-regulations-standards, same path); none of its files are in this public repository. Extracted from the CIS-published XLSX (CIS_Controls_Version_8.xlsx) via scripts/parse_cis.py. The XLSX is the authoritative source; the JSON/CSV/MD are reproducible derivatives. The source XLSX is not committed anywhere (CIS WorkBench requires registration).

notes: Originally extracted in dataset-private-laws-regulations-standards, moved to this public repository in 2026-05 on the mistaken reading that the CIS Controls are CC BY 4.0. Hosting: metadata-only in this public repository. The full text, page images, structured data and extraction scripts were removed on 2026-11-13 and are held in the private companion dataset (dataset-private-laws-regulations-standards, same path) under the 4-tier hosting rule (Kurt Seifried, 2026-11-09: free-login sources need his approval before public mirroring; paid or members-only sources are never mirrored publicly without an explicit, documented exception); this source is Tier 3 (CIS WorkBench registration required to download the source XLSX). On 2026-11-13 Kurt chose the option "Move all four (Recommended)". The content had been public here from this repository's first commit (2026-05-12) until then; it remains in git history, and whether to purge that history is a separate decision still pending. Records: CloudSecurityAlliance-DataSets/dataset-public-laws-regulations-standards#148, CloudSecurityAlliance-DataSets/dataset-private-laws-regulations-standards#15. Any return to public hosting needs an explicit, documented exception from Kurt, added as an entry in the ALLOWLIST of tools-resources/utils/check_tier_restrictions.py (a reviewed CI-gate change; see METADATA-SCHEMA.md, Public hosting exceptions).
